title: Denver Travel Guide

hero.headline: Denver Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan Denver around walkable central districts, museums, food, city parks, and carefully framed Front Range day trips.

overview: Denver is a high-plains city at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, not a mountain town itself. Its best urban itinerary combines Union Station and LoDo, the RiNo arts district, major museums, parks, and neighborhood dining, with a separate day for Front Range scenery if time allows.

The old guide blurred city attractions with regional destinations. This version keeps Denver's municipal experiences distinct from places such as Red Rocks and Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge, which are worthwhile regional outings with their own geography and management.

highlights.title: Union Station and LoDo
highlights.description: Use the historic rail hub and surrounding blocks as an orientation point for central Denver.

highlights.title: Arts and museums
highlights.description: Combine the Denver Art Museum, cultural institutions, and RiNo murals for contrasting creative districts.

highlights.title: Parks and neighborhoods
highlights.description: Add City Park, Capitol Hill, or another neighborhood rather than spending the whole trip downtown.

highlights.title: Front Range access
highlights.description: Reserve a separate block for Red Rocks or mountain scenery instead of presenting regional sites as downtown attractions.

thingsToDo.title: Start at Denver Union Station
thingsToDo.description: The restored rail station is both a transportation hub and a useful gateway to LoDo. Walk the surrounding historic blocks, continue toward Coors Field or the river corridor, and use the station's rail connections if arriving from Denver International Airport.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the RiNo Art District
thingsToDo.description: RiNo mixes murals, galleries, converted industrial buildings, food halls, breweries, and live venues north of downtown. Walk a compact section rather than trying to cover the entire district, and look for current exhibitions and events.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Denver Art Museum
thingsToDo.description: The Denver Art Museum anchors the Golden Triangle cultural area near Civic Center. Allow a substantial indoor block, then pair it with nearby architecture, the State Capitol area, or another museum rather than crossing the city repeatedly.

thingsToDo.title: Spend time in City Park
thingsToDo.description: City Park provides lawns, lakes, skyline and mountain views, and access to major attractions including the Denver Museum of Nature & Science and Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance. It is a genuine Denver urban park and a useful contrast to downtown streets.

thingsToDo.title: Take a regional trip to Red Rocks
thingsToDo.description: Red Rocks Park and Amphitheatre lies west of central Denver in the foothills and is owned by the City and County of Denver, but it is geographically outside the urban core near Morrison. Visit for the sandstone setting, amphitheatre, trails, or a performance, and plan travel time accordingly.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge
thingsToDo.description: Northeast of central Denver, this federally managed wildlife refuge protects prairie habitat on a former military-industrial site. Wildlife drives and trails can add a nature-focused half day, but it should be treated as a separate refuge rather than a downtown Denver park.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Denver works year-round, with different strengths by season
bullets: Spring and fall often provide comfortable city walking but can bring rapid weather changes.
Summer favors patios, parks, concerts, and early outdoor starts; afternoon storms can affect mountain outings.
Winter can alternate between snow and mild sunny periods, while mountain conditions are much more severe than in the city.

travelTips: Remember that Denver is on the high plains; the high mountains begin west of the city.
Use the airport rail line and central transit when they fit your itinerary, then rent a car or book a tour for regional mountain outings.
Drink water and allow time to adjust to the elevation before strenuous exercise.
Group LoDo, downtown, RiNo, and museum districts geographically to reduce unnecessary driving.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Denver?
faq.a: Three to four days allows two or three city-focused days plus a regional outdoor day.

faq.q: Is Red Rocks in downtown Denver?
faq.a: No. The park is owned by Denver but sits in the foothills near Morrison, so it requires a separate drive or tour.
Not for many central Denver attractions, especially if using airport rail and local transit. A car becomes more useful for foothill and mountain day trips.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Denver is Colorado's capital and largest city, a transportation and cultural hub on the South Platte River at the western edge of the Great Plains.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The city sits roughly a mile above sea level east of the Rocky Mountain foothills. Mountain views are central to Denver's identity, but many famous alpine destinations are well outside city limits.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Denver grew from the 19th-century mining era into a regional rail, government, business, and cultural center. Historic commercial districts now sit alongside major museums, sports venues, arts districts, and rapidly changing neighborhoods.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Urban parks and trails support walking and cycling inside Denver, while foothill amphitheatres, wildlife refuges, and mountain recreation require separate regional outings.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Central districts can be combined by walking and transit. Denver International Airport is far east of downtown but connected by rail; mountain destinations generally require road transportation.
